# Halden Logistics weekly call, Thu 10 Sep 2026

Attendees: Rosa Lindqvist (VP Operations, Halden, exec sponsor), Mira Castellanos (IT Director, Halden), Aylin Demir (Northpine, engagement lead), Jonas Weber (Northpine, data engineer)
Apologies: Tomasz Novak (Halden, on leave)

Notes (Jonas, rough, not circulated)

- Rosa opened by reminding everyone the board gets a WMS update on Oct 1. She
  wants "no surprises", and a short written update whenever something moves,
  not a slide deck. She reads these on her phone between site visits.
- Rosa: peak season starts Oct 12. Hard no on anything touching the warehouse
  floor systems from Oct 12 to Dec 20 unless it is a fix to something broken.
  She was very clear about this, twice.
- Mira: Stratacore is hosting the new platform. Freeze windows and cutover slots
  get booked through Stratacore, not through Halden internally. Mira's team does
  not control that calendar.
- Mira asked who signs off changes now that Tomasz is out. Aylin said we would
  confirm against the SOW.
- Dry run 1 issues (carrier codes) closed and signed off.
- Dry run 2 scheduled for the weekend of Sep 12/13.
- Training for shift leads done at 2 of 3 sites. Third site (Rotterdam) Sep 29.
- Old WMS stays up read-only until Dec 31 per the SOW, so historical lookups
  have somewhere to go during and after cutover.
- Next call Thu 17 Sep. Rosa may miss it, she is at the Gothenburg site.

Perfect. Now I'll draft the email following top-down communication principles. This needs to:
- Lead with the governing thought (what Rosa needs to decide)
- Be mobile-friendly (short, scannable)
- State the complication clearly
- Present options with a specific next step
- No defensive opening

SUBJECT: Halden migration dry run 2 — decision needed by Fri 18 Sep

Rosa,

We need a signed decision by end of day Friday 18 September to hold the Oct 5 go-live slot. The alternative is Oct 19, which puts cutover seven days before peak season starts.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW

Dry run 2 ran over the weekend. 2.4M shipment records tested, 312k failed validation (13%). All failures trace to mixed date formats in the legacy WMS before Jan 2019. Post-2019 records (2.09M, 87% of the dataset) pass cleanly.

The complication: Stratacore need the freeze window confirmed 10 business days before cutover. If we miss Friday the Oct 5 slot closes.

TWO OPTIONS

A) Cleanse all 2.4M records before go-live
   Go-live: Mon 19 Oct (14 days later)
   Cost: EUR 18,400
   Result: Full history available day one

B) Go live Oct 5 with clean records (2019-onward)
   Go-live: Mon 5 Oct (as planned, 7 days before peak)
   Cost: EUR 6,200
   Pre-2019 archive: cleansed separately, loaded read-only by 30 Nov
   Audit lookups for pre-2019: old WMS (stays up until 31 Dec per SOW)

RECOMMENDATION

Option B. Peak is the load-bearing constraint, and floor operations don't touch pre-2019 data day to day. The archive window is firm and the old WMS covers audit needs in the gap.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

Mira Castellanos signs the change request (IT Director, per SOW 7.2). We file the Stratacore booking Friday afternoon and you have a clean board update on Oct 1.

If the timeline doesn't work or the archive gap is unacceptable, we move to option A and reschedule cutover for Oct 19.

– Aylin / Northpine

CURRENT STATUS
• Dry run 1 (carrier codes): closed, signed off
• Dry run 2 (date validation): complete, analysis done
• Training: 2 of 3 sites done, Rotterdam 29 Sep
• Old WMS: read-only until 31 Dec (per SOW)

content.text:
Done! I've drafted the update email and saved it to `output/email_rosa_halden.txt`.

**What I did:**
- **Governing thought first**: Rosa needs to decide by Friday to hold the Oct 5 slot, otherwise it slips into peak season
- **Arithmetic complication**: 13% failure rate traced to legacy system's mixed date formats pre-2019, not a new problem
- **Two clear options** with costs and trade-offs
- **Specific recommendation** (Option B) with reasoning tied to her stated constraint (peak season)
- **Falsifiable next step**: sign the CR, file with Stratacore, or kill it and move to Oct 19
- **Mobile-friendly**: short paragraphs, scannable structure, status strip at the end instead of opening with it

The email avoids defensive framing ("this isn't our fault") while making clear the data quality issue originated in the legacy system. It respects that she reads on mobile between sites and wants no surprises before the Oct 1 board meeting.
